A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same paper. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 and the appendix report original attack evaluations, perturbation measurements, ablations and comparisons between theoretical bounds and empirical results.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by evaluations of additional watermarking methods, defenses and attack comparators.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same surrogate training, target-watermark choices, ensemble objective, gradient updates and early stopping. The mixed HiDDeN/StegaStamp ensemble used in a new experiment changes the surrogate configuration, without introducing a new attack procedure.

E1.justification: The Stable Diffusion, Midjourney and DALL-E 2 source datasets remain. However, evaluation expands beyond HiDDeN and DWT-DCT to images protected by StegaStamp, Stable Signature and smoothed watermark defenses, plus Tree-Ring under common post-processing. These substantially broaden the tested watermarking environments.

E2.justification: v3 Figures 5 and 14 add the ensemble-classifier attack MI-CWA and diffusion purification method DiffPure to the corresponding attack comparisons. The two-watermark classifier baseline is recast as AdvCls-Enc-WM1&WM2 with explicit target-encoder access. WEvade-B-S, AdvEmb-RN18 and AdvCls-Real&WM remain.

E3.justification: New experiments use equal numbers of HiDDeN and StegaStamp surrogates, regression-smoothed target models, and 100 ResNet-18 classifiers for MI-CWA. MI-CWA and DiffPure are constrained to approximately 0.9 average SSIM. The two-watermark baseline's stated access now includes the encoder. Original sample counts, attack budgets, detection thresholds and Table 1 learning rates remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds smoothed-versus-unsmoothed defense evaluations in Figure 6, common post-processing stress tests of DWT-DCT and Tree-Ring in Figure 10, and successful perturbed-image examples in Figure 1. Existing sensitivity, attack-variant and theory-versus-empirical analyses are retained, including their appendix results.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over test images without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Surrogate-training bootstrapping and the empirical estimation of theoretical bounds are retained; no new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports over 77% evasion across five watermarking targets with 100 surrogates in Figure 6, MI-CWA/DiffPure results in Figures 5 and 14, and non-learning watermark post-processing results in Figure 10. Original HiDDeN attack curves remain unchanged, while several post-processing perturbation and SSIM curves change numerically. The PDFs do not explain those numerical revisions.

T1.justification: v1 assumes equal surrogate and target watermark lengths. v3 introduces separate lengths, applies the existing reasoning to their shared bit range, and extends Theorem 3 and Appendix E with trivial bounds of zero and one for unmatched target bits. The central derivations and independence assumptions remain; their relocation to Appendix F is not new theory.

C1.justification: The central no-box vulnerability claim and three stated contributions remain. The introduction explicitly broadens the transferability claim to differing watermarking algorithms and extends the superiority claim to adversarial-example purification, beyond the earlier architecture and watermark-length comparisons.

C2.justification: v3 explains that attacks on smoothed models exceed their certified perturbation bounds, interprets MI-CWA's low success as a limitation of classifier-based transfer, and discusses DiffPure's image-quality tradeoff. It also explicitly connects expected bitwise-accuracy bounds to double-tail detection. Earlier mechanism explanations and finite-sample caveats remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies use of Meta's public Stable Signature model, the original StegaStamp architecture, regression smoothing and public DiffPure code. It also specifies the two-watermark classifier's image sources and new ensemble configurations. These add implementation information; the existing attack hyperparameters and learning-rate table are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Stable Signature, certified image watermarking, DiffPure, Tree-Ring and Liu et al.'s transferable adversarial examples, while removing the Tramèr et al. reference. Positioning against classifier ensembles becomes more explicit. Chen et al.'s ensemble-attack paper was already cited in v1; its publication update is not a new work.

P1.justification: The introduction and baseline descriptions are revised, epsilon is renamed sensitivity, the standalone transfer-adversarial-examples subsection is removed, and formal definitions and assumptions move to Appendix F. The eight-section organization and most method and results prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds an image montage and two experimental figures, expands comparison bar charts, changes several graph scales and legends, and extensively reformats typography, captions and page layout. The DWT-DCT attack plot moves to the appendix. Appendix figures now interrupt proof sequences, rather than largely following them.

improvement.justification: v1's broad claim relies chiefly on one learned watermark family and lacks an ensemble-classifier comparison. v3 addresses these important gaps through additional watermark families, smoothed defenses and image-quality-constrained MI-CWA/DiffPure comparisons. This substantially strengthens the evidence for generality and comparative effectiveness. Limited documentation of some new settings, unexplained numerical revisions and a more fragmented appendix reduce clarity but do not outweigh the gains.
